extracted.intended_audience: Florida state agencies, regulated persons, administrative law practitioners, and members of the public participating in Florida rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory requirements in Florida law governing agency rulemaking, petitions (to initiate rulemaking, hearings, variances/waivers), committee review, statements of estimated regulatory costs, recordkeeping, and publication of the Florida Administrative Code and Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in a petition for administrative hearing by a petitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for administrative hearing by a petitioner must include specific factual and legal statements describing notice, interests affected, disputed facts, ultimate facts alleged, legal bases, and relief sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically the petition must include: (a) a statement of when and how the petitioner received notice of the agency’s action or proposed action; (b) an explanation of how petitioner’s substantial interests are or will be affected; (c) a statement of all material facts disputed or a statement that there are no disputed facts; (d) a statement of the ultimate facts alleged including the specific facts petitioner contends warrant reversal or modification; (e) a statement of the specific rules or statutes petitioner contends require reversal or modification and explanation of how alleged facts relate to those rules/statutes; and (f) a statement of the relief sought stating precisely the action petitioner wishes the agency to take.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform requirements for respondent's request for administrative hearing in enforcement/disciplinary actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules must require that a respondent's request for an administrative hearing include identifying and contact information, dispute (or non-dispute) of material facts, and reference to the administrative complaint file number and receipt date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required contents: name, address, e-mail, telephone of party and counsel/representative for service; a statement either identifying disputed material facts or stating the respondent does not dispute them; and a reference by file number to the administrative complaint and the date the agency pleading was received. Agencies may provide an election-of-rights form only if it requests this information and imposes no additional requirements unless authorized by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform rules for petitions for declaratory statements and required publication notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must have uniform rules describing how petitions for declaratory statements are filed and disposed and must describe contents of notices to be published in the Florida Administrative Register, including any applicable time limits for intervention or hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules must provide prompt disposition procedures and specify what must appear in the Register notices, including time limits for petitions to intervene or administrative hearings by persons whose substantial interests may be affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to publish agency organization and operations description on agency website
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency head must provide a description of the agency’s organization and general course of operations and publish that statement on the agency’s website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform rules shall provide a method for the agency head to provide this description and the rules shall require publication on the agency website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform rules for granting or denying variances and waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must adopt uniform rules establishing procedures for granting or denying petitions for variances and waivers pursuant to s. 120.542, including emergency/temporary procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules must govern petitions for variances/waivers and may provide expedited timeframes, waiver or limited public notice, and limitations on comments for emergency or temporary grants or denials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for adopting rules substantively identical to federal regulations (adoption of federal standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: When implementing federal programs, agencies may adopt substantively identical state rules but must follow specified notice, comment, filing, and timing procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must publish a notice of intent in the Florida Administrative Register at least 21 days prior to filing and provide a copy to the committee at least 21 days prior to filing; consider written comments received within 14 days after publication; file and the rule is adopted upon filing with the Department of State; substantive changes after notice require republishing. The state rule cannot become effective earlier than the federal regulation's effective date. A substantially affected person may file an objection within 14 days specifying portions objected to and reasons; the agency must not adopt the objected portions unless it deems the objection frivolous (an objection to a rule that does not differ in any material respect from the federal regulation is deemed frivolous). When a federal regulation is invalidated, withdrawn, or substantially amended, the agency must publish repeal or may adopt the amendment within specified 60- and 180-day timeframes. Rules identical to federal regulations should reference the federal regulation whenever possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to initiate rulemaking—filing and agency response timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person regulated or with substantial interest may petition an agency to adopt, amend, or repeal a rule or to provide minimum public information; the petition must specify the proposed rule and action requested and the agency must act within prescribed timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must, within 30 calendar days of filing, initiate rulemaking proceedings, otherwise comply with the requested action, or deny the petition with a written statement of reasons. If petition directed to an unadopted rule, the agency must within 30 days either initiate rulemaking or publish notice in the FAR that it will hold a public hearing within 30 days after publication. If agency does not act within timeframes after hearing, it must publish a statement of reasons and file with the committee; the committee may hold hearings and recommend legislation. If the agency initiates rulemaking after the hearing, it must publish a notice of rule development within 30 days and file notice of proposed rule within 180 days unless it publishes a statement explaining why it did not file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking record contents and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must compile and retain a rulemaking record for all rulemaking proceedings that includes specified documents and retain the record while the rule is in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record shall include: all notices given for the proposed rule; any statement of estimated regulatory costs; a written summary of hearings; written comments and responses as required by law; all notices and findings made under subsection (4); materials filed with the committee under subsection (3); materials filed with the Department of State under subsection (3); and written inquiries from standing committees of the Legislature concerning the rule. Each state agency shall retain the record as long as the rule is in effect; when a rule is no longer in effect the record may be destroyed pursuant to approved records-retention schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for lower cost regulatory alternatives and effect on rule filing timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: A substantially affected person may submit a good faith lower cost regulatory alternative within 21 days after publication of notice; submission triggers agency duties and extensions to the rule filing timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal may include the alternative of not adopting any rule if it explains how objectives will be achieved. Submission extends the 90-day period for filing the rule by 21 days. The agency must prepare or revise its statement of estimated regulatory costs, and either adopt the alternative or provide a statement of reasons for rejecting it. Failure to prepare or respond is a material failure to follow procedures and has limited avenues for later challenge (timing/standing constraints apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: When a statement of estimated regulatory costs is required (thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency must prepare a statement of estimated regulatory costs if a proposed rule will adversely impact small businesses or is likely to increase regulatory costs in excess of $200,000 in the aggregate within 1 year after implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency must also revise the statement if any change to the rule increases regulatory costs and must provide the revised statement to the proposer of a lower cost alternative and to the committee at least 21 days before filing the rule for adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in a statement of estimated regulatory costs
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of estimated regulatory costs must contain specified economic analyses, estimates of affected parties and costs, transactional cost estimates, impacts on small businesses and small governments, and descriptions of alternatives considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required inclusions: (a) economic analysis showing whether the rule is likely to have an adverse impact on economic growth/job creation/investment, business competitiveness, or increase regulatory/transactional costs in excess of $1 million in the aggregate within 5 years; (b) good faith estimate of number and types of individuals/entities required to comply; (c) good faith estimate of cost to agency and other state/local governments and anticipated effect on revenues; (d) good faith estimate of transactional costs to individuals/entities (defined as direct, readily ascertainable costs such as filing fees, licensing costs, equipment, monitoring/reporting); (e) analysis of impact on small businesses, small counties, and small cities including basis for decision not to implement less-impactful alternatives; (f) any additional information agency finds useful; and (g) description of any regulatory alternatives submitted and a statement adopting or rejecting them with reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative submission and ratification when costs exceed statutory thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: If a rule's adverse impact or regulatory costs exceed the thresholds in the statement requirements, the rule must be submitted to the President of the Senate and Speaker of the House no later than 30 days prior to the next regular legislative session and may not take effect until ratified by the Legislature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission requirement is triggered by exceeding any of the criteria in the economic-analysis thresholds. There are specified statutory exceptions (federal standards and certain triennial code updates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and scope rules for variances and waivers (standards to grant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Variances and waivers are available where strict application of a rule would create substantial hardship or violate principles of fairness and where the person demonstrates the underlying statute's purpose will be or has been achieved by other means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial hardship is defined as demonstrated economic, technological, legal, or other hardship. Principles of fairness are violated when literal application affects a person significantly differently than similarly situated persons. Agencies may limit duration or impose conditions only to the extent necessary to achieve the underlying statute. Variances/waivers cannot be granted to statutes or federal-required rules except as allowed by the federal program or with federal approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variances/waivers—petition content, notice, timelines, and decision standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions for variances/waivers must specify the rule, action requested, specific facts justifying relief, and why the relief serves the statute; agencies must give public notice and act within set timelines; decisions must be supported by competent substantial evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must specify the rule, type of action requested, specific facts justifying waiver/variance, and how the waiver serves the underlying statute. Agency must notify Department of State within 15 days for publication in the FAR with petitioner name, date filed, rule number/nature, and how to obtain the petition; uniform rules must allow public comments. Except for emergency requests, agency may request additional information within 30 days and must review additional information within 30 days (limited follow-up requests allowed). Agency shall grant or deny within 90 days after receipt of the original petition, last timely requested additional material, or the petitioner’s written request to finish processing; failure to act within 90 days is deemed approval. Orders granting/denying must be filed with the committee and contain relevant facts and reasons; notices must be published in the FAR with specified content. Agency decisions are subject to ss. 120.569 and 120.57 and must be supported by competent substantial evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies must maintain a record of variances/waivers petitions and dispositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency must maintain a record of the type and disposition of each petition for variance or waiver, including temporary or emergency grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a required agency recordkeeping duty to track petitions and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee review criteria for proposed and existing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The legislative Administrative Procedures Committee shall examine proposed and emergency rules and may determine whether various specified defects or issues exist (delegated authority, statutory consistency, notice adequacy, cost statements, form, necessity, complexity, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific items the committee may examine include: whether the rule is an invalid exercise of delegated authority; whether statutory authority was repealed; whether the rule reiterates or paraphrases statutory material; whether the rule is in proper form; whether prior notice was sufficient to give adequate notice of purpose and effect; consistency with legislative intent; necessity to accomplish statutory objectives; reasonableness regarding public convenience; potential to be made less complex or more comprehensible; compliance of the statement of estimated regulatory costs with s. 120.541 and whether less-costly alternatives exist; whether rule will require additional appropriations; and for emergency rules whether an emergency justifies adoption and compliance with emergency rule limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee objection process, timelines for agency response, and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If the committee objects to a rule it shall certify objections within 5 days and the agency must respond within statutory timeframes depending on whether the agency head is an individual or collegial body and whether the rule is in effect; failure to respond has specified consequences including withdrawal, refusal to amend, and potential legislative action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee may request information and consult standing committees. After certification, agency has 30 days (individual head) or 45 days (collegial body) to: (if rule not in effect) file notice of modifications limited to addressing the objection, withdraw the rule, or notify refusal to modify/withdraw; (if rule in effect) file notice to amend the rule to address objection, file notice to repeal, or notify refusal to amend/repeal. If objection is to statement of estimated regulatory costs, agency must prepare a corrected statement and give notice or notify refusal. Failure to respond within required time to an objection to a not-yet-effective rule constitutes withdrawal of the rule; failure to respond to an objection to an in-effect rule constitutes refusal to amend or repeal. If agency refuses to act, committee files notice of objection with Department of State and may eventually recommend legislation; committee may request temporary suspension and, under timelines, the agency must suspend or notify refusal. A suspended rule cannot be the basis of agency action, and suspended status may expire if proposed legislation fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication duties of the Department of State—Florida Administrative Code (FAC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of State must compile and publish electronically the Florida Administrative Code containing all adopted rules and associated materials and make the electronic publication the official compilation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FAC must cite the grant of rulemaking authority and the specific law implemented for each rule, include history notes, complete indexes, and any other material required or deemed useful; department may contract for a printed publication but retains responsibility and copyright. Some local/internal rules (e.g., certain school district or internal personnel/business/finance rules) need not be published in the FAC, and exclusion does not affect validity. At the agency section start the department shall publish agency contact info, how the agency indexes its rules, listing of rules excluded from publication, and where excluded rules may be inspected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and incorporated materials—filing, incorporation by reference, and hyperlink rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms used by agencies must be filed and, when they meet the definition of a rule, be incorporated by reference with identifying information; electronic filing and hyperlinking of incorporated materials are governed by specified rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms shall not be published in the FAC, but any form used in dealings with the public must be filed with the committee before use. If a form meets the definition of a rule it must be incorporated by reference into the rule with number, title, effective date, and explanation of how to obtain it. Forms incorporated after Dec 31, 2007 must clearly display number, title, effective date, and rule number. The department shall allow adopted rules and incorporated materials to be filed electronically; when a rule is filed with incorporated electronic material, the FAC must include a hyperlink from the incorporating reference directly to that material. The department may not allow hyperlinks from FAC rules to material not filed with and maintained by the department, but may allow hyperlinks to incorporated material maintained by the department from an adopting agency’s website or other sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Florida Administrative Register (FAR) publication requirements and features
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of State must publish the Florida Administrative Register electronically containing specified notices and provide user features for search, subscription, and commenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAR must contain: all notices required by s. 120.54(2) and (3)(a) showing text of all proposed rules; notices of public meetings/hearings/workshops including how to obtain agendas; notices of requests to amend/repeal uniform rules or adopt new ones; notice of petitions for declaratory statements or administrative determinations; summaries of committee objections; lists of rules filed for adoption in previous 7 days; lists of rules pending legislative ratification; and other required/authorized material. Department may contract for printed publication. The FAR website must allow searching by type, date, rule number, word, subject, and agency; provide at least 5 years of searchable notices; allow subscription to automated e-mail notifications with summary text; allow viewing of agency forms and materials filed electronically and incorporated by reference; and allow commenting on proposed rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency obligations regarding copies, electronic notifications, style, fees, and recordkeeping for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must provide copies of rules on request with proper citations; the Department prescribes style and form; agencies pay space rates for FAR use; department maintains a permanent record of notices; agencies with e-mail notification services must use them for required notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department shall prescribe by rule the style and form required for rules, notices, and other materials submitted for filing. The Department shall charge agencies a space rate to cover FAR and FAC costs, maintain a permanent record of all notices published in the FAR, and allow agencies that provide e-mail notification services to use those services to notify licensees or registered recipients of each notice required under the referenced statute. Publication on the FAR does not preclude agency website posting or other means. Agencies shall provide copies of their rules upon request with citations to rulemaking authority and the specific law implemented.
